relations.evidence: A SQL++ error happens when there is an error processing the SQL++ statement in a request.

notable_absence.finding: The page shows two error codes and links to neither. Both are catalogued in server/current/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/n1ql-error-codes.md - 3000 as "Indicates a syntax error occurred during statement parsing" and 12003 as "Keyspace not found in CB datastore: «details»", each with a stated user action - and the page's own error messages match those catalogue entries verbatim. So the two pages agree perfectly on content and are not linked in either direction. No See Also section exists. This is the single highest-value doc fix in the batch: an error-example page whose entire purpose is to show error codes, with no route to the error-code reference.

cross_component_finding: The two examples on this page differ in an unstated but important way, and together they show that "SQL++ error" as defined here spans two very different failure phases. The first (code 3000, misspelled SLECT) is caught during parsing, before any catalogue lookup; the second (code 12003, keyspace `motel` instead of `hotel`) is caught during semantic resolution against the datastore. The elapsedTime figures corroborate the split - 1.478631ms for the parse failure against 3.096786ms for the resolution failure - but the page draws no distinction and its one-sentence definition covers both. The 12003 message also silently reveals the default query context: the statement names `travel-sample`.inventory.motel and the error reports "default:travel-sample.inventory.motel", i.e. the datastore namespace prefix `default:` is prepended. That four-part addressing is documented as n1ql:query-context / n1ql-intro:keyspace-reference in earlier rounds but is not explained here, so a reader meeting `default:` for the first time in an error message has no pointer.
version_finding: None. No version or edition marker on the page, and neither error code carries an availableSince or deprecation note. Both examples use the post-7.0 three-part keyspace form `travel-sample`.inventory.hotel and report serviceLoad in metrics, so unlike exserviceerror.md in the same directory this page's captured output is current.
